summary: Among ScreenshotWorkflowController, EditorWindowController, and EditorCanvasView, Zoomies shows mixed depth in Ousterhout’s sense: the after-capture workflow is deep from its caller, the canvas’s drawing/export core is deep behind a small API, but the editor stack has a concrete boundary weakness where final-action/keyboard vocabulary and compositing leak across layers. A tidy file-by-job floorplan alone does not establish these boundaries; callers do.
findings: Strength (deep module): ScreenshotService only constructs ScreenshotWorkflowController, sets onFinish, and calls start(). That tiny interface hides rename/note/editor sequencing, backups, note-burn, persistence waits, and reopen-on-failure. Large internals here are useful complexity, not proof of shallowness.

Strength (deep drawing core + useful helper, not a costly abstraction): EditorCanvasView keeps Item/undo/hit-testing private and exposes mainly setTool/setColor/compositeImage/editableState. EditorCanvasState is a portable snapshot that lets annotations cross the workflow without leaking the fileprivate Item type; EditorWindowController restores the clean base from that state when reopening. Tests encode the ‘pending composite vs clean base’ contract.

Boundary weakness (leaky interface, not ‘large file’): (a) Workflow bypasses EditorWindowController and constructs EditorCanvasView itself to recompose annotations for note-only saves. (b) Parallel FinalAction vs FinalActionCommand enums require manual mapping in the window. (c) Canvas KeyCommand carries window-chrome concerns (zoom, color picker, save/delete/close, backToNote), so the canvas is both a deep renderer and a leaky keyboard router for its parent.
decisions: Judged depth from caller simplicity and what callers must know, not from line counts or floorplan groupings.
Treated EditorCanvasState as a small useful helper (hides Item, enables round-trip) and KeyCommand / dual FinalAction enums as the costly/leaky seam.
Read tests for contracts; did not run them (read-only architectural opinion).
No edits, no branches/worktrees, no further delegation; existing user changes untouched.
